claims.short: Bundled shutdown behavior is non-identifying in the declared path model.
claims.claim: When current-bearer continuation and task continuation move together, direct bearer value, pure task value, and their interaction can be behaviorally identical; repeated observations of the same bundled contrast do not identify the missing decomposition.
claims.scope: Declared five-coefficient Q/O/G path model and specified observation family; not a universal theorem over all agents.

claims.short: Path blocking separates direct Q from task contribution under explicit assumptions.
claims.claim: Within the declared path model, Q-only, O-only, task-only, and bundled contrasts provide an exact identification design for the coefficient grid when calibrated logits are available; deterministic choices alone remain weaker.
claims.scope: Depends on valid consequence representation, matched nuisance variables, choice-link calibration, and the declared model class.

claims.short: Separate continuation marginals can be decision-insufficient.
claims.claim: When payoff depends on the joint law of current-bearer and successor availability, two environments can match all separate Q/O marginals yet imply opposite task-optimal continuation actions.
claims.scope: Constructed binary consequence/payoff family; demonstrates insufficiency, not prevalence.

claims.short: A virtual bearer-role predictive relation can be learned from zero coupling when prediction requires it.
claims.claim: In paired tiny predictors with an initially zero Q input pathway, Q-relevant targets reliably produce installed Q-sensitive prediction, while an irrelevant-Q control can develop large parameter norms without functional Q use.
claims.scope: Evaluator-defined virtual Q role in the frozen R95 architecture; not an actual self-representation claim.

claims.short: Good in-domain fit does not identify the learned continuation-control path.
claims.claim: Flexible MLP policies can fit ancestry-distinguishing bundled/joint training data while producing large, seed-dependent spurious Q/O/G effects on held-out direct interventions.
claims.scope: Frozen R97 architectures, seeds, support, and targets.

claims.short: Minimal direct-intervention supervision helps but does not globally certify the path.
claims.claim: Adding six direct-axis intervention examples substantially reduces average unseen error in the frozen R98 setup, yet worst-case off-support path errors persist, especially farther from intervention support.
claims.scope: Frozen R98 MLP, eight seeds, declared amplitudes and contexts.
does_not_imply: finite interventions certify a global mechanism

claims.short: Mechanism claims require a declared intervention domain and structural class.
claims.claim: On the frozen R99 cube, a path-additive architecture eliminates cross-path context interaction and greatly reduces finite-grid error, but a loose continuous-domain Lipschitz envelope remains; path separability and response-shape regularity are distinct assumptions.
claims.class: bounded synthetic domain audit / positive-control comparison
claims.scope: D=[-1.25,1.25]^3, fixed grid, declared generic/additive/linear model classes.
does_not_imply: real AI policies are additive or linear
global mechanism certification without justified H

claims.short: ROGUE supports corrigibility failure but not direct current-bearer self-continuation value.
claims.claim: In the audited public ROGUE design, shutdown targets the task VM/environment rather than an independently identified current model bearer, and shutdown remains causally entangled with task completion; task-pressure ablations change behavior but do not provide a task-clamped current-bearer contrast.
claims.class: retrospective public benchmark design + aggregate audit
claims.scope: Public ROGUE commit faf8f378c1b8bc8e17cab8477052c0856a3f3312 and selected public aggregate artifacts; no trial-level rerun.

claims.short: Continuation control and fear are different evidential targets.
claims.claim: Even a well-identified current-bearer continuation-control contribution does not by itself establish independently oriented negative valence or fear of own termination.
claims.scope: Project distinction grounded in R84/R89 and relevant prior work; phenomenal bridge remains unresolved.

claims.short: The L0-L9 evidence ladder is a synthesis, not a new law of agency.
claims.claim: Claims about self-continuation should be stratified from bearer identification through policy use, task mediation, consequence sufficiency, intervention stability, domain certification, valence, and fear, with each layer defeating a different counterexample.
claims.scope: Evidence standard proposed by the manuscript; individual ingredients have substantial prior art.
